```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

## The seasonal grower forecast for mouseforecast.com, built from the plague forecast model (Section E's 3-state
## hidden Markov model), with this season's surveys spread to nearby cells (r/e_spread_current_state.R). It replaced
## a summary of the raw survey data (r_not_in_use/raw_data_update.qmd).

library(targets)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)
library(terra)

## Targets store and r/ folder, from the project root (tar_make) or from this folder (manual render).
store_path <- if (dir.exists("_targets")) "_targets" else "../../_targets"
r_path <- if (dir.exists("r")) "r" else "../../r"
qmd_dir <- if (dir.exists("quarto_reports/mouseforecast.com")) "quarto_reports/mouseforecast.com" else "."
tar_load(c(plague_hindcast, plague_hindcast_scores, current_state_map, state_spread_scores, aez, aus_shp, surveys_all), store = store_path)
source(file.path(r_path, "a_season_info.R"))

## Town labels for map orientation, as on the current page.
town_labels <- sf::st_as_sf(
  read.csv(if (file.exists("raw_data/town_labels.csv")) "raw_data/town_labels.csv" else "../../raw_data/town_labels.csv"),
  coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = "EPSG:4326", remove = FALSE
)
names(town_labels)[1] <- "name"

theme_update(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")

## The model's three states as grower activity levels (low, moderate, high), as a traffic light: ColorBrewer's red-yellow-green end colours,
## which differ in lightness as well as hue (dark green, light amber, deep red), so they stay distinct for
## colour-blind readers and in print, unlike a bright green beside a pale yellow.
phase_labels <- c("Low", "Moderate", "High")
phase_colours <- c(Low = "#1a9641", Moderate = "#fdae61", High = "#d7191c")
```

```{r}
#| label: forecast-prep
#| include: false

## The grid hindcast's latest season (r/e_hindcast_plague_occurrence.R), which sets the season forecast below. The
## hindcast and the maps built from it are already limited to the prediction region (grain-growing land), so no
## further masking is needed.
period_key <- function(p) as.integer(sub(".*_", "", p)) * 100 + as.integer(sub("_.*", "", p))
latest <- plague_hindcast[period_key(plague_hindcast$period) == max(period_key(plague_hindcast$period)), ]
## Each cell's chance of each level once this season's surveys at nearby paddocks are taken into account
## (r/e_spread_current_state.R); cells far from any survey keep the conditions-only forecast.
cells <- current_state_map[!is.na(current_state_map$spread_1), ] |>
  mutate(phase = factor(phase_labels[max.col(cbind(spread_1, spread_2, spread_3), ties.method = "first")], levels = phase_labels),
         at_least_building = spread_2 + spread_3)
## The spread distance chosen by the pipeline (r/e_score_state_spread.R), for the text.
spread_km <- state_spread_scores$settings$bandwidth_km[1]

## The season forecast (the one after the covariates' season), for the outlook heading, figures and captions.
covariate_period <- latest$period[1]
covariate_date <- as.Date(paste(sub(".*_", "", covariate_period), sub("_.*", "", covariate_period), "15", sep = "-"))
forecast_season <- season_info(seq(covariate_date, by = "3 months", length.out = 2)[2])
## The forecast season's months with their year, e.g. "September to November 2026"; a summer spanning two
## years gets both ("December 2026 to February 2027").
season_start_text <- if (format(forecast_season$season_start, "%Y") == format(forecast_season$season_end, "%Y")) {
  format(forecast_season$season_start, "%B")
} else {
  format(forecast_season$season_start, "%B %Y")
}
season_months <- paste(season_start_text, "to", format(forecast_season$season_end, "%B %Y"))

## "a, b and c" for lists in the text.
and_join <- function(x) if (length(x) <= 1) x else paste(paste(x[-length(x)], collapse = ", "), "and", x[length(x)])

## How well the forecast warned of recorded plague years before 2013, which the model never saw, in each state
## (r/e_score_plague_hindcast.R): the chance that a state's plague year had a higher forecast chance of plague
## than one of its non-plague years (0.5 is no better than guessing).
state_skill <- plague_hindcast_scores$state_year |>
  filter(era == "hindcast") |>
  group_by(state) |>
  summarise(auc = mean(outer(occupancy_mean[flag == 1], occupancy_mean[flag == 0], ">") +
                         0.5 * outer(occupancy_mean[flag == 1], occupancy_mean[flag == 0], "==")), .groups = "drop")
## States in words: good warning from 0.7, some from 0.6, little below that.
good_states <- and_join(state_skill$state[state_skill$auc >= 0.7])
some_states <- and_join(state_skill$state[state_skill$auc >= 0.6 & state_skill$auc < 0.7])
weak_states <- and_join(state_skill$state[state_skill$auc < 0.6])
skill_text <- paste0(
  if (length(good_states) > 0) paste0("it gives good warning in ", good_states) else "",
  if (length(some_states) > 0) paste0(if (length(good_states) > 0) ", " else "", "some warning in ", some_states) else "",
  if (length(weak_states) > 0) paste0(" and little in ", weak_states) else ""
)
```

```{r}
#| label: set_issue_date

## Title block: title / tagline (the front matter's subtitle) / issue date. Quarto has no slot for a line under
## the subtitle, so the issue date is added there by JavaScript.
cat(sprintf(
  '<script>
    document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
      var sub = document.querySelector("#title-block-header p.subtitle") || document.querySelector("p.subtitle");
      var issuedLine = document.createElement("p");
      issuedLine.className = "subtitle";
      issuedLine.style.fontSize = "0.8em";
      issuedLine.style.color = "#666666";
      issuedLine.textContent = "%s";
      if (sub) sub.insertAdjacentElement("afterend", issuedLine);
    });
  </script>',
  sprintf("Issued %s", format(Sys.Date(), "%d %B %Y"))
))
```

```{r}
#| label: map-prep
#| include: false

## The map frame (as the retired raw-data page's): extent from the AE zones ever surveyed by traps or
## rapid assessment (Qld Central left out, as there) plus 1.5 degrees, and the towns shown within it.
aez_surveyed <- surveys_all |>
  filter(data_type %in% c("traps", "rapid"), !is.na(ae_zone)) |>
  pull(ae_zone) |>
  unique() |>
  setdiff("Qld Central")
map_bbox <- sf::st_bbox(filter(aez, ae_zone %in% aez_surveyed))
map_buf  <- 1.5
map_xlim <- c(map_bbox["xmin"] - map_buf, map_bbox["xmax"] + map_buf)
map_ylim <- c(map_bbox["ymin"] - map_buf, map_bbox["ymax"] + map_buf)
town_labels_crop <- filter(town_labels, longitude >= map_xlim[1], longitude <= map_xlim[2],
                           latitude >= map_ylim[1], latitude <= map_ylim[2])
## The maps' height-to-width ratio, so the figure fits the map without blank bands above and below it:
## coord_sf draws a degree of longitude cos(latitude) times as wide as a degree of latitude, so the map panel's
## own ratio is its latitude span over its longitude span times that factor.
map_panel_asp <- unname(diff(map_ylim) / (diff(map_xlim) * cos(mean(map_ylim) * pi / 180)))
## The figure's ratio at 8 inches wide: the panel (about 7.85 inches wide inside the plot margins) plus about
## 0.85 inches for the legend below.
map_fig_asp <- (7.85 * map_panel_asp + 0.85) / 8
## Town label positions outside the prediction area. Each town's label is placed at the free spot nearest the
## town: its text box clears every forecast cell, every town point, every label and leader line already placed,
## its leader line crosses no other leader line or label, and it stays inside the map's limits, so the map's
## extent is unchanged.
## Towns with the most cells around them are placed first, as they have the fewest free spots. Box sizes are in
## degrees at the maps' 8-inch width and 2.5 mm text: about 0.31 degrees of longitude per character and 0.45
## of latitude tall.
place_town_labels <- function(towns, cell_x, cell_y, xlim, ylim, char_w = 0.31, text_h = 0.45, pad = 0.1, cell_half = 0.05) {
  towns <- sf::st_drop_geometry(towns) |>
    select(name, longitude, latitude)
  ## Each label's half-width and half-height, padding included.
  half_w <- nchar(towns$name) * char_w / 2 + pad
  half_h <- text_h / 2 + pad
  ## Labels and leader lines placed so far.
  placed <- data.frame(x = numeric(0), y = numeric(0), hw = numeric(0))
  segs <- data.frame(x0 = numeric(0), y0 = numeric(0), x1 = numeric(0), y1 = numeric(0))
  ## Whether segment (ax, ay)-(bx, by) properly crosses any placed leader line (orientation test).
  orient <- function(px, py, qx, qy, rx, ry) sign((qx - px) * (ry - py) - (qy - py) * (rx - px))
  crosses_any <- function(ax, ay, bx, by) {
    if (nrow(segs) == 0) return(FALSE)
    any(orient(ax, ay, bx, by, segs$x0, segs$y0) * orient(ax, ay, bx, by, segs$x1, segs$y1) < 0 &
        orient(segs$x0, segs$y0, segs$x1, segs$y1, ax, ay) * orient(segs$x0, segs$y0, segs$x1, segs$y1, bx, by) < 0)
  }
  ## Points along a segment (20 steps), for checking it against label boxes.
  along <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 21)
  ## Whether segment (ax, ay)-(bx, by) passes through any placed label's (unpadded) text box.
  through_label <- function(ax, ay, bx, by) {
    if (nrow(placed) == 0) return(FALSE)
    px <- ax + along * (bx - ax)
    py <- ay + along * (by - ay)
    any(vapply(seq_len(nrow(placed)), function(j) any(abs(px - placed$x[j]) < placed$hw[j] - pad & abs(py - placed$y[j]) < half_h - pad), FALSE))
  }
  ## Whether a box (centre x, y; half-width hw) covers any placed leader line.
  covers_line <- function(x, y, hw) {
    if (nrow(segs) == 0) return(FALSE)
    px <- outer(segs$x0, 1 - along) + outer(segs$x1, along)
    py <- outer(segs$y0, 1 - along) + outer(segs$y1, along)
    any(abs(px - x) < hw & abs(py - y) < half_h)
  }
  ## Candidate box-centre offsets from the town, on a 0.1 degree lattice.
  offsets <- expand.grid(dx = seq(-6, 6, by = 0.1), dy = seq(-5, 5, by = 0.1))
  ## Hardest towns first: those with the most cells within 1.5 degrees.
  crowding <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(towns)), function(i) sum(abs(cell_x - towns$longitude[i]) < 1.5 & abs(cell_y - towns$latitude[i]) < 1.5), 0)
  towns$label_x <- NA_real_
  towns$label_y <- NA_real_
  for (i in order(crowding, decreasing = TRUE)) {
    tx <- towns$longitude[i]
    ty <- towns$latitude[i]
    hw <- half_w[i]
    cand_x <- tx + offsets$dx
    cand_y <- ty + offsets$dy
    ## Leader line end: the nearest point on the (unpadded) text box to the town.
    end_x <- pmin(pmax(tx, cand_x - hw + pad), cand_x + hw - pad)
    end_y <- pmin(pmax(ty, cand_y - half_h + pad), cand_y + half_h - pad)
    ## Candidates that keep the whole box inside the map and clear of the town itself, nearest first (by leader
    ## line length, ignoring the latitude stretch, which is small at these latitudes).
    keep <- which(cand_x - hw >= xlim[1] & cand_x + hw <= xlim[2] & cand_y - half_h >= ylim[1] & cand_y + half_h <= ylim[2] &
                  !(abs(offsets$dx) < hw & abs(offsets$dy) < half_h))
    keep <- keep[order(sqrt((end_x[keep] - tx)^2 + (end_y[keep] - ty)^2))]
    for (k in keep) {
      x <- cand_x[k]
      y <- cand_y[k]
      clear <- !any(abs(cell_x - x) < hw + cell_half & abs(cell_y - y) < half_h + cell_half) &&
        !any(abs(towns$longitude - x) < hw & abs(towns$latitude - y) < half_h) &&
        !any(abs(placed$x - x) < placed$hw + hw & abs(placed$y - y) < 2 * half_h) &&
        !crosses_any(tx, ty, end_x[k], end_y[k]) &&
        !through_label(tx, ty, end_x[k], end_y[k]) &&
        !covers_line(x, y, hw)
      if (clear) {
        towns$label_x[i] <- x
        towns$label_y[i] <- y
        placed <- rbind(placed, data.frame(x = x, y = y, hw = hw))
        segs <- rbind(segs, data.frame(x0 = tx, y0 = ty, x1 = end_x[k], y1 = end_y[k]))
        break
      }
    }
  }
  ## Each label's leader line: from the town to the nearest point on its (unpadded) text box.
  towns |>
    mutate(seg_x = pmin(pmax(longitude, label_x - half_w + pad), label_x + half_w - pad),
           seg_y = pmin(pmax(latitude, label_y - half_h + pad), label_y + half_h - pad))
}
town_label_pos <- place_town_labels(town_labels_crop, cells$x, cells$y, map_xlim, map_ylim)
## The grain-growing area's edge as one outline, traced around the forecast cells themselves so it follows
## their square edges exactly.
cell_grid <- terra::rast(data.frame(x = cells$x, y = cells$y, value = 1), type = "xyz", crs = "EPSG:4326")
grain_outline <- sf::st_as_sf(terra::as.polygons(cell_grid, dissolve = TRUE))
## A forecast map in that frame: the grid layer (one fill column) between the Australian outline and the towns.
forecast_map <- function(fill_col, fill_scale) {
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = aus_shp, fill = "white", colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_raster(data = cells, aes(x, y, fill = .data[[fill_col]])) +
    fill_scale +
    ## The grain-growing area's edge in black over the grid, so its cells stand out from the land around them
    ## (including near-white cells on the chance map).
    geom_sf(data = grain_outline, fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.25) +
    ## No axis titles (an empty "" title still takes up a line of space).
    labs(y = NULL, x = NULL) +
    geom_sf(data = town_labels_crop, size = 0.75) +
    ## Town labels at their placed positions outside the prediction area, each with a line back to its town.
    geom_segment(data = town_label_pos, aes(longitude, latitude, xend = seg_x, yend = seg_y), linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_text(data = town_label_pos, aes(label_x, label_y, label = name), size = 2.5) +
    coord_sf(xlim = map_xlim, ylim = map_ylim, expand = FALSE) +
    theme(legend.box.margin = margin(b = -8), legend.justification = "center", legend.box = "vertical",
          ## Little space between the map and the legend, and only a little below the legend.
          legend.box.spacing = unit(4, "pt"), plot.margin = margin(5.5, 5.5, 6, 5.5),
          ## No coordinate ticks or labels: the town names orient the reader.
          axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank())
}
## Figure 1's caption, also saved for the email draft.
cap_phase <- paste0("Most likely level of mouse numbers in ", forecast_season$label, " predicted across key grain-growing areas (shown at a 10 × 10 km spatial resolution). \"Low\" numbers reflect typical yearly fluctuations in mouse numbers, with \"moderate\" numbers rising above normal levels where crop damage is possible (potentially in a build-up phase), and \"high\" approaching or at concerning numbers where crop damage is likely. The forecast is based on past mouse surveys, environmental conditions in the previous season, and this season's surveys at nearby paddocks.")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-phase
#| fig-asp: !expr map_fig_asp
#| fig-cap: !expr cap_phase

p_phase <- forecast_map("phase", scale_fill_manual(values = phase_colours, drop = FALSE, name = paste("Estimated level of mouse numbers in", forecast_season$label),
                                                   guide = guide_legend(title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5)))
## A copy of the map and its caption for the email draft (email_draft.qmd), which embeds them as they are.
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(qmd_dir, "email_map.png"), plot = p_phase, width = 8, height = 8 * map_fig_asp, dpi = 150, bg = "white")
writeLines(cap_phase, file.path(qmd_dir, "email_caption.txt"))
p_phase
```

## Report mouse activity

Take 60 seconds to report mouse activity on your farm on [MouseAlert](https://feralscan.org.au/mousealert).

We are primarily seeking observations from within paddocks (not houses or farm sheds), and particularly encourage reporting of low activity – not just observations of high mouse activity. This helps both inform and validate our forecasts.

## About

Mouse forecasts are enabled through a [Grains Research and Development Corporation and CSIRO investment into the 2025–29 Mouse Monitoring and Surveillance project](https://groundcover.grdc.com.au/grdc/announcements/investments-target-new-normal-of-mouse-activity) via the [Rodent Management team](https://research.csiro.au/rm/). Forecasts will be updated seasonally or as new data becomes available.

We are actively testing and improving the statistical forecast model, and working on its presentation. This work is coordinated with the National Mouse Group, a grower-led network of farmers, industry representatives, state government, GRDC and CSIRO. The group meets three times a year to share local reports of the current mouse situation, review management recommendations and determine research priorities.

### Monitoring data
Mouse population surveys are conducted 3–4 times a year at each of the ~170 long-term monitoring sites.
Mice are surveyed through active burrow searches and chew cards. To calibrate this data against more robust population density measurements, we also conduct live-trapping at 4 sites (Adelaide Plains SA, Northern Mallee VIC, Central West NSW and Moree NSW).

Mouse monitoring data is collected by CSIRO, NSW Local Land Services, NSW Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development, Central West Farming Services, Birchip Cropping Group, and Farmanco. We also thank NSW DPIRD, who generously provide additional live-trapping survey data. Further live-trapping data is occasionally supplied through the [GRDC / CSIRO Mouse Ecology 2024–2029 project](https://research.csiro.au/rm/research-projects/mouse-ecology-2024-2029/).

We also receive reports from farmers, agronomists and other community members directly. These reports are valuable, as we cannot feasibly survey every paddock across the grain-growing region.

### How the forecast works

- **A statistical model.** Built on more than 40 years of mouse surveys (live-trapping, active burrow counts and chew cards), it estimates whether mouse numbers in each area are most likely low, moderate or high this season.
- **Three abundance levels.** Numbers move from low to moderate after conditions turn good, and from moderate to high most often after a sharp dry-to-wet swing. Both fall back to low when good conditions end.
- **What drives predictions.** Recent mouse survey data and environmental conditions: satellite crop growth, soil moisture, rainfall swings, temperature, soil type.
- **How far ahead.** One season, as it uses observed conditions, not weather forecasts.
- **How reliable.** Tested against plague years recorded before 2013 (records it was not trained on), `r skill_text`. It can't yet be tested in Western Australia, which lacks reliable plague records for that period.
- **How to interpret.** The forecast shows regional risk, not individual paddocks, and will sometimes miss an outbreak or give a false alarm, so use it as a prompt to check your own paddocks.

### Contact {#sec-contact}

Questions about the forecast? Get in touch with Dr Matthew Rees at [matt.rees@csiro.au](mailto:matt.rees@csiro.au).

For media enquiries, contact Research Officer Steve Henry ([steve.henry@csiro.au](mailto:steve.henry@csiro.au)) or the [CSIRO media office](https://www.csiro.au/en/news/Media-Centre).

We value your feedback.

::: {.no-print}

```{=html}
<!-- JSONP submission keeps the user on this page and shows inline feedback.
     The form action is only used as a no-JS fallback. -->
<form id="mailchimp-form"
      action="https://mouseforecast.us20.list-manage.com/subscribe/post?u=952eafef177b5f80f3265bedd&id=ebb485fa13"
      method="post" class="mt-3">

  <div class="mb-2">
    <input type="email" name="EMAIL" class="form-control"
           placeholder="Email address" required>
  </div>

  <!-- Mailchimp bot-protection honeypot (must stay hidden and empty) -->
  <div style="position: absolute; left: -5000px;" aria-hidden="true">
    <input type="text" name="b_952eafef177b5f80f3265bedd_ebb485fa13" tabindex="-1" value="">
  </div>

  <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary w-100">Subscribe</button>

  <!-- Submission status shown here by the script below -->
  <div id="mailchimp-result" class="mt-2" style="display:none;" role="alert"></div>


</form>

<script>
(function () {
  var form = document.getElementById("mailchimp-form");
  if (!form) return;

  form.addEventListener("submit", function (e) {
    e.preventDefault();

    var resultEl = document.getElementById("mailchimp-result");
    resultEl.className = "mt-2 alert alert-info";
    resultEl.textContent = "Subscribing\u2026";
    resultEl.style.display = "block";

    /* Collect form fields into a query string */
    var data = new FormData(form);
    var params = [];
    data.forEach(function (value, key) {
      params.push(encodeURIComponent(key) + "=" + encodeURIComponent(value));
    });

    /* Unique callback name avoids collisions if submitted twice */
    var cbName = "mc_cb_" + Math.round(Math.random() * 1e8);

    /* Mailchimp JSONP endpoint: /post-json + &c=CALLBACK_NAME */
    var url =
      "https://mouseforecast.us20.list-manage.com/subscribe/post-json" +
      "?u=952eafef177b5f80f3265bedd&id=ebb485fa13&" +
      params.join("&") + "&c=" + cbName;

    /* Mailchimp calls this function with the response object */
    window[cbName] = function (resp) {
      if (resp.result === "success") {
        resultEl.className = "mt-2 alert alert-success";
        resultEl.textContent = "Thank you for subscribing!";
        form.reset();
      } else {
        /* Strip any HTML tags Mailchimp includes in the message */
        var msg = (resp.msg || "Something went wrong. Please try again.")
                    .replace(/<[^>]+>/g, "");
        resultEl.className = "mt-2 alert alert-danger";
        resultEl.textContent = msg;
      }
      delete window[cbName];
    };

    /* Inject a <script> tag — this is how JSONP works */
    var s = document.createElement("script");
    s.src = url;
    s.onload  = function () { if (s.parentNode) s.parentNode.removeChild(s); };
    s.onerror = function () {
      resultEl.className = "mt-2 alert alert-danger";
      resultEl.textContent = "Network error. Please try again.";
      delete window[cbName];
      if (s.parentNode) s.parentNode.removeChild(s);
    };
    document.head.appendChild(s);
  });
})();
</script>
```
